incidents.vector: Attackers weaponized a public proof-of-concept for CVE-2026-10520, a max-severity (CVSS 10) OS command injection flaw in the Ivanti Sentry mobile gateway, to gain unauthenticated root code execution within 24 hours of disclosure.
incidents.impact: Researchers observed non-stop exploitation against internet-facing Sentry appliances, with at least two instances already backdoored; compromise exposes stored credentials and directory connections and enables lateral movement.

incidents.vector: An external actor accessed university systems and exfiltrated data; the ShinyHunters extortion group claims it stole over 40GB of material including payment card and personal records.
incidents.impact: The university confirmed a 'significant amount' of current and former student data was accessed; analysis of leaked data found ~455,000 unique email addresses plus names, addresses, passport numbers, ethnicities, disabilities and fee-payment details.

incidents.vector: Suspected Chinese intelligence operatives ran at least 13 fake consulting-company websites with AI-generated personas and photos, posting 'consulting' jobs on hiring platforms to recruit current and former clearance holders into disclosing sensitive information.
incidents.impact: The DOJ and FBI seized the 13 domains used since November 2023 to lure Americans with payments for 'insider' reports; the operation was disrupted, though officials warn the broader Chinese recruitment effort continues.

incidents.vector: The Qilin ransomware operation is actively exploiting a vulnerability in Check Point remote-access tools, firewalls and VPNs that act as gatekeepers to corporate networks.
incidents.impact: CISA gave U.S. federal agencies just three days to patch the bug under active attack; successful exploitation provides ransomware operators an entry point into protected networks.

incidents.vector: Microsoft's record 206-CVE June Patch Tuesday included CVE-2026-41091, a Windows Defender elevation-of-privilege flaw already exploited in the wild (added to CISA's KEV catalog May 20), while researcher 'Nightmare Eclipse' kept publishing working zero-day exploit code for Windows Defender and BitLocker.
incidents.impact: The actively exploited Defender bug lets an attacker with a foothold seize full system control; public PoC drops (RoguePlanet and a BitLocker bypass) force emergency patching, with the researcher threatening further releases on July 14.

incidents.vector: Operators likely based in China used ChatGPT to generate images and fake-American social media posts amplifying divisive U.S. debates over data centers, electricity prices and tariffs, posing as Americans on X and YouTube.
incidents.impact: OpenAI disrupted two clusters ('Data Center Bandwagon' and a tariff-themed network) and rated them 1-2 on its breakout scale, finding no evidence of meaningful audience engagement.

incidents.vector: A Russian disinformation group known as Matryoshka hijacked Bluesky accounts to post pro-Kremlin, anti-Ukraine propaganda, with the activity running since April.
incidents.impact: Bluesky has been suspending compromised accounts until owners can re-secure them; part of a broader Russian influence push also targeting Armenia's elections.

incidents.victim: U.S. businesses, universities and NATO-region organizations
incidents.vector: A Russia-aligned espionage group authenticated to victim cloud accounts using stolen session tokens to bypass re-authentication, then masked connections through U.S.-based commercial proxies and typosquatted Microsoft login domains.
incidents.impact: U.S. prosecutors charged Russian national Denis Obrezko for buying the VPS and domains used in the campaign; the FBI verified intrusions at 11 U.S. companies, likely a fraction of the total, with bulk email, files and Teams chats harvested.

incidents.vector: Iran-linked hackers breached the website of an independent all-female news agency operating out of Türkiye, deleting articles and disrupting online broadcasts.
incidents.impact: The actors took credit for the hack and threatened to dox and harm employees, part of a wider pattern of Iranian proxy operations against perceived adversaries.

incidents.vector: A new spear-phishing operation tried to lure WhatsApp users into clicking malicious links leading to an external site, in violation of a U.S. court injunction barring NSO from targeting Meta's platform.
incidents.impact: Meta detected and disrupted the campaign and filed a contempt complaint against NSO, urging lawmakers to keep the spyware maker on U.S. sanctions lists.

incidents.vector: Attackers abused an API bug to access data from ServiceNow customer instances; the flaw was quietly patched but had reportedly been exploited since at least April.
incidents.impact: ServiceNow notified affected customers, with incidents mainly impacting its Australia platform release.

incidents.victim: U.S. law, professional and financial services firms
incidents.vector: The UNC3753 cluster (aka 'Luna Moth'/'Silent Ransom Group') used invoice-themed lures and IT-helpdesk vishing to convince employees to install RMM tools and screen-sharing software, then located and exfiltrated sensitive files — in some cases sending operatives into offices to steal data via USB in person.
incidents.impact: Dozens of organizations were hit, often with theft-to-extortion completed in under a business day; the group issues aggressive three-day extortion demands and threatens to publish stolen legal agreements, PII and financial records on its leak site.

incidents.victim: Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS / GlobalProtect users
incidents.vector: An unidentified actor actively exploited CVE-2026-0257, an authentication bypass in PAN-OS GlobalProtect portal and gateway components, to initiate unauthorized VPN connections (added to CISA's KEV catalog May 29).
incidents.impact: Unit 42 observed widespread probing with a portion of devices establishing gateway-connected sessions; no post-access lateral movement was confirmed, and organizations are urged to hunt for indicators and patch.

incidents.vector: Operation FlutterBridge spread the new FlutterShell backdoor through hundreds of Google-verified malvertising ads and shell companies, delivering trojanized but functional macOS apps (podcast and PDF viewers) signed with valid Apple Developer IDs that passed notarization.
incidents.impact: FlutterShell hijacks Chrome to push ads while providing shell command execution, file-system access and environment-variable exfiltration; some variants route documents through an attacker server using AI summarization for data theft. Samples had zero VirusTotal detections at analysis.

incidents.victim: Red Hat npm ecosystem / software developers
incidents.vector: Using a compromised Red Hat employee GitHub account, attackers pushed malicious orphan commits that triggered CI/CD workflows to publish at least 32 trojanized packages under the @redhat-cloud-services npm namespace with valid SLSA provenance — a 'Mini Shai-Hulud' payload called Miasma.
incidents.impact: The malicious versions averaged ~80,000 weekly downloads and harvest GitHub/npm/SSH tokens, AWS/GCP/Azure credentials, Kubernetes and Vault secrets and CI/CD secrets, then self-propagate; public release of the worm source code has spawned copycats.

incidents.vector: Pro-Iran hackers tricked Meta's AI customer-support bot into adding an attacker email to target accounts via the password-reset flow, using a VPN IP near the target's hometown to bypass checks.
incidents.impact: The Instagram accounts of the Obama White House and the Chief Master Sergeant of the U.S. Space Force were briefly defaced with pro-Iran content; Meta pushed an emergency patch and said no back-end database was breached.

incidents.vector: Hackers accessed Oxford University's CareerConnect platform at the end of May and stole data belonging to alumni, research staff and employers.
incidents.impact: The university disclosed the breach of the recruitment portal used to connect students and staff with employers about internships and jobs.

incidents.vector: A GitHub employee installed a malicious 'Nx Console' VS Code extension that had been compromised in the upstream TanStack supply-chain attack, giving attackers access to internal assets.
incidents.impact: More than 3,800 internal code repositories were exfiltrated and offered for sale on a hacking forum; GitHub rotated critical secret tokens, and Grafana linked a related hack to the same TanStack incident.

incidents.vector: Dutch financial-crime investigators arrested the co-owners of hosting firms (the[.]hosting / MIRhosting) that took over the technical infrastructure of EU-sanctioned ISP Stark Industries Solutions, used to stage DDoS, influence and disinformation operations for Russia.
incidents.impact: Authorities seized more than 800 servers and charged two men with sanctions violations; reviewed data showed the networks were the most-used in pro-Russian attacks on Danish government bodies around the November 2025 municipal elections.

incidents.victim: U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
incidents.vector: A CISA contractor published AWS GovCloud keys and a large trove of other agency secrets to a public GitHub account.
incidents.impact: CISA is still struggling to contain the breach and invalidate the leaked credentials; lawmakers in both houses of Congress are demanding answers and a classified briefing.
